PullRequest.Title: actionWidget: fix: resume interrupted IME searches
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Resume an asynchronous ActionList search that IME composition interrupted, even when composition ends with the original query. Do not repeat searches that already completed or failed, and do not let a stale request's cleanup disturb a newer request.

This is a focused follow-up to [#328269](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328269). The shared-component fixes are separated from [#335018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335018) so the automation changes can be reviewed and landed independently.

Only two files change:

- [actionList.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/66fb14d02a916676638641c6e0c21749253487a6/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts): the existing filter-input guard and asynchronous request cleanup.
- [actionList.test.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/66fb14d02a916676638641c6e0c21749253487a6/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts): four regression cases using the existing widget helpers and deferred promises.

## Background and failure

ActionList can filter an existing list locally or delegate filtering to an asynchronous provider through `onFilter`. For asynchronous filtering, it owns the current request's cancellation token source in a `MutableDisposable`.

The existing IME handling deliberately defers filtering during composition. Intermediate input can contain uncommitted text, and rebuilding or laying out the result list can disrupt the IME candidate window. Starting a composition also cancels an outstanding search so its results cannot update the list during composition.

Both `compositionend` and the accompanying `input` event eventually use the same value-change handler. That handler originally skipped every unchanged query to deduplicate those events.

The failure occurs when:

1. The user searches for `release`, starting an asynchronous request.
2. IME composition starts before the request finishes, cancelling that request.
3. Composition ends with `release` again, either after intermediate text or without a committed change.
4. The unchanged-query guard suppresses a replacement request, while the original request's results are correctly ignored because it was cancelled.

The pending query therefore never supplies fresh results until the user changes the search text again.

## How the fix works

### 1. An unchanged query can restart an interrupted request

The input handler still ignores all changes while composition is active. Outside composition, it skips an unchanged query only when there is no cancelled current request.

This lets `compositionend` restart the search that composition interrupted. The restart immediately replaces the cancelled token source with a live one, so the trailing `input` event for the same text does not issue another request. Existing checks continue to reject results from the cancelled request.

### 2. Settled requests stop looking like pending work

Relaxing the guard alone would introduce an unnecessary retry: previously the current token source remained stored after a search completed or failed. A later `compositionstart` could cancel that already-settled source and make the unchanged query look interrupted.

The asynchronous chain now has a `finally` handler that clears the token source only when:

- it is still the widget's current request; and
- it has not been cancelled.

The same cleanup runs after success or failure. Clearing through the existing `MutableDisposable` disposes the source without cancelling an already-settled token, so later composition cannot mark that search as interrupted.

The identity check is essential: an older request can settle after a newer request has replaced it. Its cleanup must not clear the newer request's cancellation state. Otherwise composition could neither reliably cancel nor restart the newer request.

A cancelled current request intentionally remains available as the retry signal, even if its promise has already settled. The existing replacement, hide, and disposal paths own its cleanup; no additional collection or long-lived listener is introduced.

## Scope and preserved behavior

- Local/static filtering remains unchanged.
- Composing text still does not drive filtering or intermediate list updates.
- Searches whose committed query changes still follow the existing request path.
- Completed and failed searches are not retried solely because composition leaves the query unchanged.
- Superseded results remain ignored, and superseded completions cannot clear newer request state.
- The existing error-handling behavior is preserved; this does not introduce a retry policy for failed searches.
- No public API, settings, commands, keybindings, labels, ARIA roles, styling, or layout rules change.
- No automation, Agents Window, or chat-picker production code is included.

The interaction remains focused and consistent: the IME retains ownership during composition, and only the interrupted committed query resumes afterward. This is not a visual redesign or a new interactive surface.

## Validation

Standalone validation against the main-based branch:

- `npm run transpile-client` succeeded and generated fresh output containing both fixes.
- **192 tests passed** across the five modules below.
- Both commits passed the normal pre-commit hygiene hook.
- `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/tabbedActionListWidget.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionWidgetDropdown.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatInputPicker.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
```

The new regression cases cover:

1. An interrupted search is restarted once when composition leaves the query unchanged; stale results stay hidden and the replacement results appear.
2. A successfully completed search is not retried or marked cancelled by a later unchanged composition.
3. A failed search is not retried or marked cancelled by a later unchanged composition.
4. Settling an older, superseded request does not lose the pending request's ability to be cancelled and retried by composition.

The tests explicitly send the trailing `input` event to verify deduplication. The existing suites also cover composition suppression, stale-result handling, keyboard and combobox behavior, disposable cleanup, and the two dynamic consumers.

Validation used synthetic browser composition events in the Electron unit runner. A native operating-system IME session and manual screen-reader pass were not rerun for this extraction.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed fall-through, immediate request creation, ignored token, 200 ms coalescing window, JSON-RPC boundary, and uncached Git subprocess fan-out are all directly traced. Exact user frequency and Git duration vary, which affects severity, but not the concurrency mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: When a dynamic search takes longer than successive unchanged IME composition cycles, every cycle that reaches compositionend after the 200 ms delayer starts another request; concurrent stale work grows linearly with the number of cycles. For branch completion, each request launches at least three and up to five uncached Git subprocesses.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Concurrent stale RPC/Git work can contend with the replacement search, increasing picker result latency and subprocess/CPU load in slow or large repositories.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The prior unchanged-value guard returned for every compositionend whose committed text matched `_filterText`, so after the first request was cancelled no replacement RPC or Git work was launched for repeated unchanged composition cycles.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new condition deliberately falls through whenever the stored request token is cancelled, and `_applyOrUpdateFilter` immediately creates a replacement request. The two production delegates ignore the supplied cancellation token, so cancelling the ActionList request only suppresses its result and does not stop the underlying completion RPC.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1082 changes an unchanged cancelled query from an unconditional return into a call to `_applyOrUpdateFilter`; before this line, the same compositionend could not launch another provider request.
Findings.Title: Cancel the stale search before restarting it
Findings.Impact: In a dynamic branch picker on a repository where completion is slow, repeatedly starting and cancelling IME composition without changing the query can leave multiple branch scans running at once. The useful replacement waits behind contention from stale scans, while the agent host executes 3–5 Git commands per scan.
Findings.Evidence: `onFilterValueChanged` now restarts the same text when `_filterCts` is cancelled (line 1082), and `_applyOrUpdateFilter` invokes the delegate immediately after the consumer's 200 ms Delayer. Both `AgentHostChatInputPicker` and `AgentHostSessionConfigPicker` define `onFilter` without the cancellation-token argument, then call `sessionConfigCompletions`/`getSessionConfigCompletions`; neither completion API accepts a token. `AgentHostProtocolClient.sessionConfigCompletions` sends JSON-RPC, and `WorktreeIsolation.branchCompletions` executes `getBranches`, `getCurrentBranch`, and `getDefaultBranch` in parallel. `AgentHostGitService` implements these as uncached Git invocations (`for-each-ref`, `branch --show-current` with fallback, and `symbolic-ref` plus up to two `show-ref`s). The added regression test also leaves the first DeferredPromise unresolved when the second request is created, directly demonstrating overlap.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the IME restart, but ensure it cannot overlap stale backend work: forward the ActionList cancellation token through the dynamic picker delegates and completion protocol/Git implementation, or sequence/coalesce same-query retries so at most one underlying provider search is active.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local/static ActionList filtering during IME composition
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input/compositionend synchronously filters the in-memory item array, splices the list, and requests layout; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible ActionList item count and committed input events; unchanged compositionend/input pairs remain deduplicated because there is no `_filterCts`.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work only; no asynchronous provider or concurrent operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; filtering scans the current in-memory items. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `_applyOrUpdateFilter` still branches directly to `_applyFilter` when `onFilter` is absent, and the changed guard still returns for unchanged text without a cancelled token.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Item counts vary by widget, but this PR does not add work to the static path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; local filtering behavior and boundary count are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dynamic ActionList search interrupted by an unchanged IME composition, including agent-host branch/config pickers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After compositionend, the changed guard starts a replacement dynamic search. The production pickers debounce it for 200 ms, then await completion RPC and result conversion before ActionList can display fresh rows. Stale requests are off the semantic critical path but remain active and can contend with the replacement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a JSON-RPC `sessionConfigCompletions` request to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per accepted dynamic filter after 200 ms debounce. The diff adds one request for each unchanged composition cycle whose current ActionList token was cancelled; cycles within one pending debounce window coalesce, but cycles after a task starts can overlap without a limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An unchanged compositionend always returned, so this interrupted-query path launched no replacement RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The newest request must complete before fresh picker rows display; stale requests do not provide rows but compete for transport and host resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read all local branch refs, current branch, and default branch using Git commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each branch-completion RPC starts three parallel Git service reads, implemented as at least 3 and up to 5 Git subprocesses. With N slow unchanged-composition retries after prior debounce tasks have started, effective subprocess work is 3N–5N and may overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Git fan-out was launched after an unchanged interrupted composition because the old guard suppressed the replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The replacement waits for its own Git fan-out; uncancelled stale fan-outs can increase latency through CPU, disk, and process contention.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and cadence of unchanged IME composition cycles while completion latency exceeds the interval between cycles; branch count also controls `for-each-ref` output and filtering work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The ActionList token cancels result consumption, but both production delegates ignore it and completion APIs accept no token. RPCs and their Git fan-outs therefore overlap without sequencing or backpressure once successive debounced tasks have started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Completion results and Git branch/current/default reads are not cached. The 200 ms Delayer coalesces only triggers before a task starts; once in flight, another trigger creates a separate task. The session picker’s dynamic-label map stores labels only and does not satisfy completion queries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added condition, delegate call flow, Delayer behavior, protocol request, and uncached Git implementations are all explicit, and the regression test demonstrates two unresolved requests coexisting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated unchanged compositions and repository Git latency vary across users, so severity is medium; the overlap and subprocess multiplicity are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable concurrency-burst regression: preserve restart semantics but cancel or sequence stale backend work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Composition after a dynamic search has already completed or failed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The original provider request settles; the added `finally` clears the current non-cancelled CTS. A later unchanged composition performs no provider work and returns immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Agent-host dynamic picker completion providers reached from IActionListDelegate.onFilter
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamic completion request for the original typed query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request before and after the diff; no retry after settlement because `_filterCts` is cleared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The original request ran once. Its settled CTS remained stored, but the unchanged guard still prevented another request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the original request is on the result critical path; later unchanged composition adds no boundary delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of completed or failed searches and later unchanged compositions; effective provider-call cardinality remains one per actual changed query.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No overlap is introduced after settlement. The identity check prevents an older request’s `finally` from clearing a newer request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache; the new CTS cleanup acts as settled-state tracking and prevents a false interrupted-request retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on the identity and cancellation checks in the added `finally` and dedicated tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the mechanism; tests cover success, failure, and superseded completion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; cleanup avoids unnecessary retries and retains only a cancelled current CTS as the restart signal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Widget hide/disposal with a cancelled dynamic filter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hide notifies the delegate, cancels and clears the current filter CTS, and disposes widget resources. This is not on search-result progress after dismissal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One current CTS per widget regardless of prior request count; completed promise closures release older CTS objects.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Clearing the ActionList CTS does not abort provider boundaries that ignore the token, but hide/cleanup behavior itself is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. A cancelled CTS may remain until replacement, hide, or disposal, but cancellation disposes its listener emitter and storage is bounded to one current source.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from `MutableDisposable` replacement/clear semantics and `CancellationTokenSource` disposal behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying provider duration varies, but no new retention collection or cleanup loop is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent cleanup-lifecycle finding; retained state is bounded and existing hide/disposal ownership remains intact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced input, cancellation, promise cleanup, both dynamic picker consumers, debounce behavior, JSON-RPC, and branch Git fan-out. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity concurrency-burst finding; static filtering and settled-request cleanup introduce no additional regressions.
